key_test: one-way between-subjects ANOVA, ambivalence = mean(StrongMixed, -NotTorn, Indecisive-4) on Condition (0 neutral, 1 one-sided, 2 two-sided); omnibus F(2,67); eta^2 = SS_cond/(SS_cond+SS_err)
exclusions: Include == 1 (identical to SexOffender == 'No'): 19 of 89 excluded; one included participant lacks Indecisive and gets the mean of the other two items

r_script.how: RPP_79dey.R run unchanged in R 4.6.2 except library(httr), library(RCurl) and source(getOSFfile.R) dropped and getOSFfile() mapped to the downloaded 3xv8u file (run_audit.R)

notes: Anchored on the script and table; the SAS syntax of the replication team runs the same omnibus (proc glm ambiv=condition) on the same exclusion. The script's imputation line Data[49,33] <- (Data[49,22]+Data[49,22])/2 uses StrongMixed twice instead of StrongMixed and reversed NotTorn; it gives the right value (1) only because that participant has StrongMixed = 1, NotTorn = -1. Python uses SAS mean-of-available semantics instead, same number. Dropping that participant: F(2,66)=1.51, p=.229. The script's Data$Include works only through R's partial matching of $ on the column 'Include..0.No..1.Yes.'. Second plausible test (the effect description names one-sided vs two-sided only): t(44) = -1.24, p = .222. The full data file henderson.replication.data.dat has 97 rows vs 89 here; not reconciled, the analysis file is the one the script and table use.
